title: Collaborating with WHIPIC in Korea?
content:
While in Sarawak, Malaysia, I connected with the International Centre for Interpretation and Presentation of World Heritage Sites (WHIPIC) which is a UNESCO Category 2 Centre and part of UNITWIN fostering global university networks to enhance teaching, research, and knowledge sharing.

WHIPIC is committed to upholding the UNESCO’s spirit of reconciliation, coexistence, and peace for all. It was established to promote the understanding and protection of World Heritage globally through inclusive heritage interpretation and presentation.

The 1972 World Heritage Convention commits signatories to the “transmission to future generations of cultural and natural heritage situated on its territory” (Art, 4). In 2015, the task of contributing to sustainable development was integrated into the processes of the World Heritage Convention.

This is recognised by WHIPIC which is dedicated to capacity building. A logical task for the future, which we have been talking about, is training for ways of representing the interests and needs of future generations in interpretation and presentation of World Heritage properties.
